title: NGINX string-prefix location /api also matches /apix (preserve or refuse)
claims: location /api (no trailing slash) keeps nginx string-prefix semantics: /api/x and /apix both reach the backend
a shorter path (/ap) is not forwarded
not_claimed: behavior of a bare /api request with a URI-bearing proxy_pass
source_semantics: nginx prefix locations are plain string prefixes, not path-segment prefixes, so /api matches /apix. Ferrum's literal prefix routes walk segment boundaries (docs/routing.md, 'segment-boundary HashMap walk'; inferred from docs, not observed), so emitting listen_path /api alone may route /apix to 404. That must be preserved or refused with a report error.
